prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent watercolour washes over it, a muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good printed picture book. NOT neon, NOT 3D or CGI or Pixar, NOT glossy plastic, NOT neo-comic, NO HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, NOT photoreal. PORTRAIT BOOK COVER for a children's picture book.

MIRA, a girl of about TEN, dark hair in a blunt CHIN-LENGTH BOB with a straight fringe, a MUSTARD-YELLOW KNITTED CARDIGAN over a plain RUST-RED DRESS, bare knees, scuffed CREAM CANVAS SHOES. She stands in the lower third of the frame on a low concrete step in a mown back garden, seen from slightly below, ONE ARM RAISED and just released, looking UP and away with plain open delight. PIP, a SMALL HAND-MADE TIN-TOY ROBOT only KNEE-HIGH to her: a round dented tin head slightly too big for its body, two round dark glass eyes, a small round brass grille below them, one small amber bulb on top, a boxy tin torso with a rust-red hinged panel, two stubby brass arms with THREE-FINGER hands, two short stubby legs. No glow, no screens, no chrome. Pip stands at her feet looking up too.

Above them the upper two thirds of the frame is WARM LATE-AFTERNOON SKY. THE SKY IS FULL OF PAPER PLANES AND NO TWO ARE THE SAME FOLD: long thin darts, short fat ones, blunt-nosed ones, broad square ones, ones with upturned wingtips, one with a thick folded-over nose, some folded from PRINTED paper with type visible. They are at every height and angle, NOT in formation, NOT evenly spaced.

BAKED TITLE LETTERING, integrated into the design at the TOP of the cover, in a warm hand-lettered serif in deep ink brown, reading EXACTLY and ONLY this string, spelled exactly: 'It Only Has to Fly'. Below it, much smaller, in small caps, reading EXACTLY and ONLY: 'A HYPERAGENTIC AGE story'. NO other text, NO author name, NO publisher, NO taglines, NO invented words, NO numbers. Spell both strings perfectly.

ONE single continuous full-bleed painting. Never a grid, never panels.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
